lower_bound.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample within the construction: take n=2 and split the pieces u,2u,4u into u; 1.05u,0.95u; and 2.1u,1.9u. The sorted parts are 2.1u,1.9u,1.05u,u,0.95u. Thus G has three vertices and two edges: a loop at the 4u vertex and an edge joining the 2u and u vertices. Hence |E|=2<3=|V|, yet G has a loop. In particular the component containing vertex n is not a simple tree and cannot receive the asserted proper two-colouring with opposite signs on the loop.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The subsequent signed-sum estimate requires the component containing n to be a loopless tree so that every paired edge has oppositely signed endpoints. The proof provides no alternative treatment of cyclic or loop components.

parsed.notes: The closed form is correct. The reduction and upper-bound construction are valid, but the claimed all-n lower-bound proof relies on a false graph-theoretic inference.
